questions: Have you noticed rapid, involuntary movements of your eyes?
Do your eyes ever drift or turn out of alignment without you intending them to?
Do you experience double vision?
Does your vision become blurry or shaky during these episodes?
Do these eye movements occur even when you are not deliberately looking to the side or upward?
Did these symptoms begin suddenly?
Have they been getting worse?
Do the episodes come and go?
Do you have dizziness or a spinning sensation?
Do you have nausea or vomiting with the eye movements?
Do you have headaches?
Have you recently had a head injury?
Have you had weakness, numbness, trouble speaking, difficulty walking, or loss of coordination?
Have you had any recent fever or infection?
Have you started taking any new medicines or recreational drugs?
Have you ever had similar eye movements before?
Does anyone in your family have involuntary eye movements or a diagnosed eye-movement disorder?
Have you noticed hearing loss or ringing in your ears?
Do you have a history of thyroid disease?
Have you had any recent change in vision in either eye?
results: 1. paraneoplastic and autoimmune antibody panel (serum): anti-Homer3 antibodies POSITIVE
2. CSF metagenomic sequencing: eight sequences of HUMAN HERPESVIRUS 7
3. immunotherapy trial: dizziness and gait improved with immunotherapy; relapse prompted rituximab, with partial improvement
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Anti-Homer3 antibody–associated autoimmune cerebellar ataxia (autoimmune cerebellitis), likely triggered by human herpesvirus 7 infection

ALTERNATIVE: HHV-7–associated infectious cerebellitis

ALTERNATIVE: Paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration with an occult malignancy

ALTERNATIVE: Other antibody-negative autoimmune cerebellar ataxia
